title: Geometric irreducibility can be tested on finite separable extensions
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $R$ a commutative $k$-algebra, meaning a commutative ring equipped with a homomorphism $k\to R$. Form tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] with multiplication $(r\otimes a)(s\otimes b)=rs\otimes ab$ and unit $1\otimes1$. The following are equivalent: (1) for every field extension $L/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], $\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_kL)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components]; (2) for every finite separable algebraic field extension $E/k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], $\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_kE)$ is irreducible. Here finite means finite-dimensional as a $k$-vector space [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], and irreducible includes nonempty. No finite-generation or reducedness assumption on $R$ is imposed.
